evidence_chain: [Fact from provided brief] Domino's is classified in this funnel as a reference benchmark, not an underfollowed candidate.

[Fact from provided brief] The relevant Domino's capabilities to verify are procurement scale, supply-chain control, menu and store standardization, first-party digital ordering, loyalty, advertising efficiency, and delivery-channel control.
[Inference from provided brief] The key chokepoint is organizational and system-level execution inside a scaled franchise model, not a scarce upstream supplier.

[Fact from provided brief] The benchmark thesis weakens if supply-chain margins compress, franchisee opening returns deteriorate, U.S. same-store sales weaken, third-party delivery dilutes economics, or loyalty engagement fades.

[Fact from cached Serenity methodology] The Serenity process starts from the theme, breaks the chain into demand drivers, supply-chain nodes, bottlenecks, public-market mappings, evidence, pricing checks, and falsification plans.

[Fact from provided external evidence: Shake Shack Q1 2026 shareholder letter] Shake Shack reported 14.3% year-over-year revenue growth, 4.6% same-Shack sales growth, 1.4% traffic growth, restaurant-level profit margin of 21.2%, margin expansion despite low-teens beef-cost increases, and digital guest count/app-download growth of more than 35%. This provides a peer reference that restaurant winners are also using supply-chain productivity, labor management, process optimization, and digital engagement as margin and traffic levers. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1620533/000162053326000024/a1q26shareholderletter.htm

[Fact from provided external evidence: Krispy Kreme Q1 2026 presentation] Krispy Kreme highlighted refranchising, margin improvement, positive free cash flow, U.S. logistics outsourcing completion, strategic partner growth, digital sales, and supply-chain disruption risk including single-source or limited suppliers. This supports the broader theme that restaurant economics can be shaped by franchise mix, logistics design, digital sales, and supplier concentration. Source: https://s202.q4cdn.com/983903322/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/DNUT-Q126-Final-Earnings-Presentation.pdf

[Fact from provided external evidence: Santiago & Company 2026 article] Independent restaurants may face procurement pressure from foodservice consolidation, with independent full-service restaurants described as having thin net margins and dependence on broadline and cash-and-carry channels. This reinforces the relevance of procurement scale as a structural advantage for large systems like Domino's and as a pressure point for smaller operators. Source: https://www.santiagocompany.com/insights/why-foodservice-consolidation-now-threatens-independent-restaurant-economics

[Hypothesis] If Domino's procurement and supply-chain system allows franchisees to absorb food-cost volatility better than less-scaled peers, then similar but smaller public-market candidates may exist in foodservice distribution, cooperative purchasing, restaurant software, logistics outsourcing, or compliance/testing nodes.
falsification_plan: Check the latest Domino's 10-K and 10-Q for supply-chain revenue, supply-chain operating margin, store count, U.S. same-store sales, international performance, and franchise segment disclosures. Falsify or downgrade the benchmark thesis if supply-chain economics weaken without clear franchisee benefit.

Review the latest earnings-call transcript for U.S. order count, ticket, traffic, loyalty engagement, digital mix, and third-party delivery commentary. Falsify if sales are mainly price-driven while traffic and order frequency decline.
Track net store openings, closures, and franchisee investment requirements. Falsify if openings slow materially or closures rise in a way that indicates weaker unit returns.

Compare Domino's food-cost and procurement commentary with peers such as Shake Shack, Krispy Kreme, and other franchised restaurant systems. Falsify if Domino's no longer shows evidence of procurement or operating leverage relative to peers.

Evaluate delivery-channel economics, including whether third-party delivery is incremental and profitable. Falsify if third-party delivery materially cannibalizes first-party ordering or reduces customer-data control.
Track loyalty activity, not just enrolled members. Falsify if active users, frequency, or digital repeat behavior weakens despite promotional investment.
Assess whether advertising contributions translate into measurable traffic or order growth. Falsify if advertising spend rises while franchisee-level sales and margins deteriorate.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: For Domino's itself, the hidden signal is whether procurement and supply-chain scale are improving franchisee economics rather than merely supporting corporate revenue. Specific signals to verify: supply-chain revenue and margin, franchisee food-cost trends versus peers, U.S. same-store sales composition, order count versus ticket growth, net store openings and closures, franchisee capex and cash returns, loyalty active-user engagement, digital ordering mix, third-party delivery contribution after commissions and operating costs, and advertising-fund efficiency. For the broader Restaurants theme, the second-order signal is whether smaller suppliers, distributors, restaurant software vendors, group purchasing platforms, inspection/compliance vendors, or outsourced logistics providers can capture similar economics without requiring the brand scale of Domino's.
next_research_tasks: Retrieve Domino's latest Form 10-K and latest Form 10-Q; extract supply-chain revenue, supply-chain margin, U.S. franchise revenue, company-owned store metrics, store counts, and segment operating income.

Read the latest two Domino's earnings-call transcripts; code management commentary into categories: traffic, ticket, order count, loyalty, digital mix, third-party delivery, franchisee profitability, food costs, and advertising.

Build a peer table using Domino's, Yum Brands, Papa John's, Wingstop, Restaurant Brands International, Shake Shack, and Krispy Kreme. Compare franchise mix, supply-chain ownership, digital ordering mix, same-store sales, traffic, net unit growth, and restaurant-level or franchisee margin proxies.

Map second-order public-market candidates that sit one or two steps away from Domino's model: foodservice distributors, group purchasing organizations, restaurant POS/software vendors, loyalty vendors, delivery/logistics enablers, food safety/testing providers, and packaging/ingredient suppliers.

Use Domino's as the benchmark scorecard: for each underfollowed candidate, ask whether it helps restaurants improve procurement cost, labor productivity, order frequency, digital customer ownership, compliance, logistics reliability, or franchisee ROI.

Search for smaller public companies with USD 300M-10B market cap exposure to restaurant procurement, distribution, software, outsourced logistics, food safety, or equipment maintenance; require explicit evidence-to-verify before promoting any candidate beyond hypothesis.
Monitor whether independent restaurant procurement pressure from foodservice consolidation increases demand for cooperative purchasing, regional distributors, or restaurant cost-control software.
risks: [Risk] Supply-chain margin deterioration could indicate that the system is losing leverage or absorbing cost pressure without sufficient franchisee benefit.
[Risk] U.S. same-store sales could weaken due to traffic or order-count decline, not just temporary mix, weather, timing, or promotional effects.
[Risk] Franchisee economics could deteriorate if required capex rises, labor costs increase, food costs outpace pricing power, or delivery economics worsen.
[Risk] Third-party delivery partnerships could create incremental revenue but dilute margin, weaken first-party customer data, or shift bargaining power toward delivery platforms.
[Risk] Loyalty engagement could decline despite marketing spend, reducing the value of first-party digital ordering infrastructure.
[Risk] Advertising-fund efficiency could fall if promotions drive traffic only at the expense of franchisee profitability.
[Risk] Food-cost inflation could narrow the procurement advantage versus peers if suppliers regain pricing power or if competitors use alternative procurement channels.
[Risk] As a high-attention large-cap stock, much of the quality and scale advantage may already be reflected in market expectations.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Restaurant-system reference leader. Position: downstream consumer restaurant brand plus franchisor infrastructure layer. Relevant nodes include ingredient procurement, dough and food distribution, franchisee support, store operating standards, digital ordering, loyalty, delivery channel management, advertising fund allocation, and unit-level economics. In Serenity terms, Domino's is not the hidden bottleneck itself; it is the operating model used to test whether procurement scale and digital/supply-chain infrastructure create measurable franchisee advantages.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 【推论】Domino's 在本轮餐饮主题中不应被当作低关注候选，而应被当作参考标尺。它的核心研究价值不是寻找一个稀缺供应商瓶颈，而是验证一个成熟加盟餐饮系统如何通过采购规模、垂直或半垂直供应链能力、门店标准化、第一方数字订餐、忠诚度体系、广告基金效率和配送渠道控制来改善加盟商单店经济。若这些能力持续转化为美国同店销售、订单频次、净开店、加盟商回报和供应链利润的稳定性，Domino's 就可以作为筛选其他餐饮基础设施、供应链、软件、分销和加盟系统候选公司的 benchmark。由于它是高关注大盘公司，直接误定价空间可能小于更隐蔽的供应链、软件、分销和运营工具型公司。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] Domino's should not be treated as an underfollowed candidate in this restaurant funnel; it should be used as a reference benchmark. Its research value is not a scarce-supplier chokepoint, but a test case for how a mature franchised restaurant system can use procurement scale, vertically or semi-vertically integrated supply-chain capabilities, standardized operations, first-party digital ordering, loyalty, advertising efficiency, and delivery-channel governance to reinforce franchisee unit economics. If these capabilities continue to translate into U.S. same-store sales, order frequency, net unit growth, franchisee returns, and stable supply-chain profitability, Domino's becomes a useful benchmark for screening smaller restaurant infrastructure, supplier, software, distributor, and franchise-system candidates. Because Domino's is a well-followed large-cap company, the direct mispricing opportunity is likely lower than in more obscure supply-chain, software, distribution, and operating-tool companies.
deep_reports.title_cn: Domino's：餐饮加盟系统的规模采购、供应链和数字化标尺
deep_reports.title_en: Domino's: Benchmark for Restaurant Franchise Procurement, Supply Chain, and Digital Ordering Economics
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed at the stock level. It is a high-attention, large-cap restaurant company. The potentially underappreciated research angle is its role as a reference model: the market may focus on same-store sales and headline consumer demand, while the Serenity funnel uses Domino's to identify which capabilities smaller or less-followed restaurant companies need to prove, including procurement leverage, supply-chain margin stability, loyalty engagement, first-party customer data, advertising efficiency, delivery economics, and franchisee return on invested capital.

evidence.claim_supported: Serenity methodology requires starting from a theme, mapping demand drivers and supply-chain nodes, identifying chokepoints, linking to public-market candidates, checking evidence, and defining falsification plans.

Domino's is a reference benchmark rather than an underfollowed candidate; key areas to verify include procurement scale, supply chain, first-party digital ordering, loyalty, advertising efficiency, delivery economics, and franchisee unit economics.
Restaurant operators are using labor management, supply-chain productivity, process optimization, premium menu innovation, and digital engagement as levers for traffic and margin performance.

Restaurant economics can be influenced by refranchising, logistics outsourcing, digital sales, strategic partner growth, leverage reduction, and exposure to supply-chain disruptions or limited suppliers.
Procurement scale and supplier concentration are relevant structural issues in restaurant economics, especially for independent operators with thin margins and limited alternatives.

Smaller restaurant concepts may depend heavily on third-party vendors, distributors, delivery services, mobile apps, and operating execution; this supports the broader Serenity search for less-visible restaurant infrastructure dependencies.

downgrade_triggers: Supply-chain margin deterioration without franchisee benefit.
Weak U.S. same-store sales driven by traffic/order-count decline.
Slowing franchisee openings or rising closures.
Third-party delivery dilutes profitability or weakens first-party customer data.
Loyalty engagement declines despite marketing investment.
memory_update.key_takeaway: Use Domino's as the restaurant-system benchmark for procurement scale, supply-chain control, first-party digital ordering, loyalty, advertising efficiency, delivery governance, and franchisee economics. Do not let DPZ crowd out underfollowed supplier/software/distribution candidates in later funnel layers.
upgrade_evidence_needed: Latest DPZ 10-K/10-Q confirms stable or improving supply-chain economics.
Earnings calls show healthy U.S. order count, traffic, loyalty engagement, and profitable digital/delivery mix.
Net unit growth and franchisee returns remain strong despite food, labor, and delivery cost pressure.

summary: Layer 5 mini deep report for the Restaurants theme. Domino's Pizza Inc. is treated as a high-attention reference benchmark, not an underfollowed alpha candidate. The research value is to use Domino's as a control case for testing which restaurant-system capabilities actually improve franchisee economics: procurement scale, supply-chain control, standardized operations, first-party digital ordering, loyalty, advertising efficiency, and delivery-channel governance. Key claims beyond the supplied brief and cached Serenity methodology are labeled as inference or hypothesis unless supported by the provided evidence context.
